status: development/regression set. Prompts, plans and scores were inspected while building it, so it must not be reported as a held-out test set. A final test set needs new prompts and action combinations, frozen before evaluation.
source: https://github.com/HapticGen/hapticgen-dataset (user_prompt). The source provides prompts and A/B votes only; every structural annotation below is ours. expertvoted prompts were used to train/fine-tune HapticGen.
selection: Rule: unique prompts (case/whitespace-normalised) of <= 40 words with an explicit count (once|twice|thrice|<number> times/taps/knocks/steps/shots/beats/clicks/hits) or a sequence connective (then|followed by|and finally|until|after that|afterwards); excluded non-contact audio captions (speech, animal calls, music) and 'once' meaning 'at once'. Items marked selection=manual were kept outside that rule; the reason is given.
annotation_status: Revised draft (v2) following the eval_set_v1 review. Explicit conditions only; interpretive conditions and rendering conventions are not scored. Still requires researcher confirmation and ideally a second independent annotator.

scoring.unit: Conditions apply to the sub-events matched by an event pattern, never to the global number of short segments. A sub-event matches an event if its prompt matches `pattern` (case-insensitive regex) and not `exclude`. Object+verb alternatives use lookaheads, so word order does not matter; an object name alone never matches an action.
scoring.count: number of sub-events matching the event equals `count` (only where the text states the count of that action and one occurrence maps to one sub-event).
scoring.order: events listed in `order` match distinct sub-events in strictly increasing start order (greedy). order_strength=weak is reported but not scored.
scoring.period: all consecutive gaps between matched sub-events within target_s * (1 +- tol_rel); requires >= 3 matched sub-events. tol_rel fixed a priori at 0.2.
scoring.relative: intensity of the first sub-event matching `stronger` exceeds that of the first matching `weaker`.
scoring.forbid: no sub-event matches any forbid pattern (content not stated in the text).
scoring.last_event: the last sub-event by start time matches this event (nothing vibrates after it).
scoring.renderable: reported separately as feasibility; never averaged with semantic checks.

items.prompt: To dribble a basketball forcefully once
After sticking and aiming the gun, he shoots at the enemy once.
A situation where I shake a tree 3 times and an apple falls on my head
items.notes: Shake count (3) is explicit but one shake need not be one sub-event; not scored.

items.prompt: clap loudly once.
He tries to break the rough wooden stick by bending it twice, but to no avail. On the third attempt, with a strong impact, the stick finally snaps.
items.notes: Two failed bends + third attempt with snap. Bend count and global strongest-last not scored.

items.prompt: He was feeling so upset that he crumpled the paper forcefully three times and slammed it to the ground.
items.notes: Crumple count (3) explicit but one crumple may be several waveform peaks or one sub-event; not scored.

items.prompt: I'm typing a document quickly on my keyboard, and then I slowly click my mouse once
I type a document on my keyboard and click my mouse once
items.notes: 'and' does not fix strict order; order reported but not scored.

items.prompt: the sound of dribbling a soccer ball in three steps
items.notes: 'three steps' may describe footsteps or progression, not three ball contacts; count not scored.

items.prompt: water bomb pops and splashes once as I hit the enemy
items.notes: Splash may be part of the same event or a sustained tail; not required as a separate contact.

items.prompt: I have been bitten twice by mosquitoes on my right hand and it's itchy
items.notes: Itch is a separate sensation and is not counted.

items.prompt: I have to do CPR. heavily and strongly pressing his chest constantly with the speed of pressing 100 times in a minute
items.notes: Total number of presses and duration are not stated.

items.prompt: Driving a racing car on a rainy day then suddenly losing control of the car and crash into a tree.
items.notes: Rendering driving as a sustained segment is a design convention; not scored.

items.prompt: riding a bike on a smooth track and then ride on a gravel field
riding a bike on a smooth track and then ride on a bumpy road
The ambulance passing outside the window approaches and then moves away.
items.notes: Approach then recede would need an envelope check under stated observer/rendering assumptions; no semantic check scored (feasibility only).

items.prompt: Trying to open a tightly shut pickle jar and then finally opening it with a loud pop.
items.notes: 'loud' does not establish the pop as globally strongest; not scored.

items.prompt: an arrow that is penetrating a melon in slow motion, starting from its hard shell into the soft fruit within and then coming out of the outer shell again
A graduate student rigorously typing their computer keyboard to write a research draft and then hitting the enter key after each paragraph, then pause..
items.notes: Number of paragraphs/Enter presses not stated. Final pause: nothing vibrates after the last Enter.

items.prompt: A swimmer swims in butterfly stroke. The swimmer repeats the process of strongly coming out of the water with both of his arms, then going back into the water.
items.notes: Repetition count not stated; two arms are not two separate contacts.

items.prompt: Dribbling a basketball then an opponent forcefully slaps the ball out of your hand with a large splat
Dribbling a basketball then an opponent slaps the ball out of your hand
Driving a truck really fast on a highway during a heavy snowfall and then crashing into a huge moose.
Feeling hungry as my stomach first rumbles softly, then contracts with a louder growl, almost like a burp.
First, I'm zipping and opening the pencil case. Then I am stirring the pencil case looking for the pencil. Then I found it and zipped the pencil case back to close it.
In a very competitive car racing game, you crash into another car, making a very large sound. Then, there is only silence.
items.notes: One crash event; silence after it (no later engine, driving or contacts). Silence length not stated.

items.prompt: I pulled back the extremely taut bowstring with all my strength and then released it, sending the arrow flying.
items.notes: Arrow flight may exist as a physical stage without vibration. Hitting a target is not stated.

items.prompt: I pulled back the extremely tense bowstring with all my strength to the fullest and then released it.
The badminton rally continued at a fast and steady pace until the game ended with a powerful smash.
items.notes: Number of rally hits not stated; 'powerful' is not scored as globally strongest.

items.prompt: Trying to open a crinkly vinyl snack package, then finally tearing it open with a sharp, crisp rip.
Trying to open a vinyl snack package, then finally tearing it open with a sharp sound.

items.selection: manual: no rule connective ('at once' excluded as a count); kept as a near-variant of s05
items.prompt: When a well-compressed and packed new pickle container is turned, it does not open even with a strong force, but when it opens at once with a cheerful puff

items.selection: manual: 'Once you fall' is a temporal conjunction, which the exclusion rule would remove; kept as a no-contact case
items.prompt: You are about to bunjee jump. Once you fall, you slice through the wind which makes a very large noise. The jump ends, and there is no more wind.
items.notes: Whether no-contact flight is rendered as vibration is a project policy; only presence of the wind event is scored.
